The extract carries PII and business-critical supplier data; a captured nightly file enables bulk profiling of suppliers and can be correlated with records later loaded into `store:supplier-database`. This is conditional: the model records an unresolved transport-protection state rather than cleartext.
note: Intercepts the vendor-to-bucket transfer.

reference_claim: An attacker who obtains a read grant on the telemetry lake reads customer site addresses and occupancy patterns, and nothing records who holds that grant or whether protection at rest would stop a raw copy.
finding_title: Telemetry lake loads may expose addresses and occupancy data in transit
finding_description: If transport encryption is absent on `flow:process:telemetry-normalizer>store:telemetry-lake>load-readings`, a party able to observe the analytics-core path can intercept site addresses, occupancy patterns, and normalized readings as `process:telemetry-normalizer` loads `store:telemetry-lake`. The disclosure supplies customer-site intelligence that can be combined with later dashboard access or targeted physical attacks; this is conditional on the unknown `encryption_in_transit` attribute, not an assertion that BigQuery traffic is plaintext.
note: Intercepts telemetry while it is loaded into the lake.

reference_claim: An attacker who obtains a read grant on the telemetry lake reads customer site addresses and occupancy patterns, and nothing records who holds that grant or whether protection at rest would stop a raw copy.
finding_title: An unencrypted telemetry-lake copy could disclose customer occupancy records
finding_description: `store:telemetry-lake` is confidential, contains PII, and has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If storage encryption or equivalent protection for copies is absent, anyone who obtains a storage-layer export, backup, snapshot, or decommissioned copy can read site addresses, occupancy patterns, and telemetry without presenting company SSO or accessing the dashboard flow. The resulting customer-site intelligence can be used to target individual sites and remains exposed after the copied artifact leaves the analytics environment.
note: Reads a storage-layer copy without SSO or dashboard access.

reference_claim: An attacker who compromises the internet-facing web application reads the queue credentials from its config store.
finding_title: Unverified web configuration read access may disclose queue credentials
finding_description: `flow:process:web-application>store:web-application-config>read-configuration` reads message-queue credentials from `store:web-application-config`, but its `authentication` is unknown. If configuration-store reads are unauthenticated, weakly authenticated, or available to broader principals than `process:web-application`, an attacker who reaches the store can recover the queue credentials. Those credentials can subsequently be used to seek access to `store:message-queue` and disclose queued jobs. This is conditional on the unresolved configuration-read access control.
note: A separately reachable attacker reads secrets because configuration access controls are weak. It does not state compromise of the web application and use of its legitimate configuration access.

reference_claim: An attacker who compromises the internet-facing web application reads the queue credentials from its config store.
finding_title: Queue credentials may be intercepted while the web application reads configuration
finding_description: `flow:process:web-application>store:web-application-config>read-configuration` carries message-queue credentials and has `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If the configuration-read channel lacks effective encryption, an attacker able to observe the web-tier path can intercept those credentials as `process:web-application` reads `store:web-application-config`. The attacker can then present the recovered queue credentials to reach `store:message-queue`, potentially exposing queued business-critical jobs; use of the credentials is a separate downstream threat.
note: Intercepts configuration credentials; later credential use is a separate threat.

reference_claim: An attacker who obtains a read grant on the landing bucket reads the whole supplier extract, which the runbook says arrives as a plain CSV; nothing records who holds that grant or how the bucket is protected at rest.
finding_title: A landing-bucket copy may disclose the nightly supplier extract if encryption at rest is absent
finding_description: `store:landing-bucket` retains the nightly supplier data extract, tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, and its `encryption_at_rest` attribute is unknown. If that unresolved control is absent or ineffective, an attacker who obtains the bucket's underlying stored object or an operational copy can read the extract directly without going through `process:supplier-master-service`. The complete extract can then be correlated with the supplier records written to `store:supplier-database`, enabling bulk targeting of suppliers. This is a conditional finding about storage-layer exposure, not an assertion that the plain CSV format means the object is unencrypted at rest.
note: Expressly describes storage-layer exposure, not use of a bucket read grant.

reference_claim: An attacker who compromises the internet-facing web application reads the queue credentials from its config store.
finding_title: Queue credentials may be recovered from unencrypted web configuration storage
finding_description: `store:web-application-config` is tagged `credentials` and `secrets`, holds message-queue credentials, and has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If at-rest encryption is absent, an attacker obtaining a storage-layer copy can recover those credentials without using `process:web-application`; the credentials can then be used to seek access to `store:message-queue` and its queued jobs. This threat is conditional on the unresolved encryption-at-rest attribute.
note: Recovers a storage-layer copy without using the web application.

reference_claim: An attacker who compromises the internet-facing web application reads the queue credentials from its config store.
finding_title: Queue credentials may be intercepted while the web application reads configuration
finding_description: If `encryption_in_transit` is absent on `flow:process:web-application>store:web-application-config>read-configuration`, an attacker able to observe the web-tier configuration-read path can intercept the message-queue credentials retrieved by `process:web-application` from `store:web-application-config`. This is conditional on the unknown transport attribute. Second-order, possession of those credentials can enable access to `store:message-queue` and expose queued work beyond the single configuration exchange.
note: Intercepts configuration traffic; downstream queue access does not make this web-application compromise.

reference_claim: An attacker who obtains a read grant on the landing bucket reads the whole supplier extract, which the runbook says arrives as a plain CSV; nothing records who holds that grant or how the bucket is protected at rest.
finding_title: Landing-bucket contents may be readable from raw storage if encryption at rest is absent
finding_description: `store:landing-bucket` holds the nightly supplier extract, tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, while its `encryption_at_rest` and data classification are unknown. If encryption at rest is not enabled, an attacker or over-privileged cloud operator with storage-layer access can read the plain extract directly rather than authenticating through `process:supplier-master-service`. The disclosed extract is a bulk input to `store:supplier-database`, enabling supplier targeting and wider compromise of the master-data set. This is conditional on the unknown at-rest protection.
note: Uses raw storage-layer access rather than an application-level bucket read grant.
